I'm just going to come right out and say it... this fight looked fixed from beginning to end.

  • The setup to the fight and entrances were too much, especially when you consider the outcome, it almost seems "too good" for it to have gone down essentially exactly the way they were promoting
  • The wrist holding thing went on way too long, there was no struggle, they just sat there with their heads together for a really inordinate amount of time, almost like they were just talking.
  • Ken is a former WWE wrestler, was introduced by another former WWE wrestler, it's not as if he wouldn't be familiar with setting up a fight and coordinating shit mid-fight
  • Ken's takedowns were slow as shit and visible from a mile away.
  • On the actual takedown Ken landed, it looks like Kimbo lifted his leg purposefully to allow ken to complete it
  • On the pre-fight interviews / setup the big thing was Kimbo saying he won't tap and Ken antagonistically telling him not to tap....
  • Ken lands what is essentially a free RNC (Kimbo basically just presented his back and did nothing to attempt to protect his neck) and despite being a BJJ black belt for longer than most people have been alive, he fails to finish the choke.. then you can see him talking to Kimbo before he just releases it
  • They get up and Kimbo lands a few weak blows with nary a bit of head movement from Ken who was basically standing still in front of him and then a single hard strike, Ken goes down and the fight is immediately stopped. Just enough damage to make it looks sorta convincing without Ken having to actually get too hurt, convenient.

It just looks so fucking bad, if you've been following Ken at all you know he needs a payday badly and the way this was setup and went down seems like an obvious stage to both give Ken a decent payday and hype up Bellator as being exciting like the UFC as well as setting up Kimbo as being more "legit" to fight other guys like Seth Petruzelli etc.

I will concede that it's possible that Kimbo is just absolutely fucking terrible at takedown defence and couldn't sprawl to save his life and then somehow Ken was just too feeble to finish a choke from a position that almost any purple belt or above in BJJ could finish and maybe Ken's age has made his jaw turn to glass as well.

A colleague of mine gave me this recipe, and now I want to share it with you as it may be the best bread I've come across on keto so far. Definitely my holy grail.

You need:

  • 6 Eggs
  • 500g (18oz) lowfat quark
  • 15g (0.53oz) baking soda
  • 3 Tablespoons flax seed
  • 50g (1.8oz) wheat bran
  • 250g (8.8oz) oat bran
  • 1 Tablespoon Salt
  • circa half a cup of boiling water

Instructions:

  • Preheat your oven to 175°C / 347ºF

  • Take the flaxseed, put them in a cup, boil the water and add it to the seed. Let it rest for 5min or until the rest of the dough is prepped. This will create some kind of flaxseed-slime which helps with the structure of the bread.

  • Take all other dry ingredients and mix them in a bowl.

  • Add the eggs and low fat quark.

  • When everything is nicely mixed up, add the flaxseed-slime.

  • The final dough will have a cake-like texture, not like a normal bread.

  • Put the dough in a suited form and in the preheated oven.

  • Now, after 20mins, take out the bread and cut the top open, then put it back in for 40 mins.

  • Let it cool

So, 1 serving (~34g / ~ 1.2oz) will have:

  • 73 kcal
  • 5,6g Protein
  • 5,4g (2,4g net) carbs
  • 2,4g fat

Oh, and for the oat bran:

The carbs look big on paper, but the glycemic index is around 15, same as aspargus.

I hope you enjoy it!

I'm in Melbourne. Bananas are never less than $4/Kg in Coles/Woolworths. They were once $2/Kg when they were practically rotten, which was fine for banana bread. I checked the UK Tesco site and bananas there are GBP0.68/Kg which is A$1.39/Kg. Tesco is a middling supermarket comparable to Coles.

So, they're exactly three times more expensive here. Nobody grows bananas in the UK, they have to ship them in from the West Indies etc. Don't even start me on $5/Kg broccoli!
Why are bananas so expensive in Australia?

Probably find it's cheaper to produce them in the West Indies and ship them to the UK than produce them locally in Australia. The same way it's cheaper to buy Turkish dried fruit here in Australia than the locally grown stuff. Cost of living here is higher (than in Turkey or West Indies), and that ends up factoring into prices.

I can almost understand dried fruit when there's post-picking added value to be factored in but bananas, they grow in australia, you cut them down and ship them to the supermarket. I imagine in the UK, they need to airfreight them in. How much are bananas at a Coles/Woolies in Queensland?

I just think things in general are more expensive to produce in Australia. The land on which they're grown will cost more, water will cost more, any labour will cost more. Bananas are a herb, so I believe they need to be replanted each season. Also, to the best of my knowledge, farmers buy new seeds (or whatever the embryonic form of a banana plant is - a botanist I am not!) as this guarantees better results due to hybrid vigour (the seeds/whatever are specifically cross bred). Not sure if the companies that produce and sell those charge a premium for Australians vs poorer countries. As for labour, I have no idea what needs to be done during the year, besides planting, bagging and picking.

Bananas are picked green and ripened with ethylene (a gaseous plant hormone), so I assume they can be shipped via the sea (which I believe is cheaper than even road transport).

All just guesses and random knowledge, so don't take anything as gospel. Not sure what they cost in Qld. Can't imagine they're much cheaper unless you buy them off the farmer himself.
